title: Persatrix Security Configuration (v0.3.12+)
description: Internal-only schema until v1.0; `$id` may break across v0.x bumps without notice. The `auth:` block (RFC 0039 §H + the enabled-mode exposure amendment §A/§B) governs the REST/console authentication surface: the disabled/enabled rollout switch, session TTLs per transport, Argon2id cost, the two login limiters, and the trusted reverse proxies for per-source key resolution. The Go loader (internal/server/auth_config.go) is the semantic authority — this schema is the `make validate` authoring gate; a file that passes here can still fail the loader's cross-field checks.

mode.description: The RFC 0039 §H rollout switch. `disabled` (default): every request resolves to the anonymous `local` identity, no route enforced, pre-RFC behaviour byte-for-byte. `enabled`: identity resolution live; the §E policy matrix enforces from Phase 2. Any networked deployment MUST set enabled.

session_ttl.description: Bearer-transport session lifetime (Go duration syntax; minimum 1s). The CLI / programmatic-caller TTL.

cookie_session_ttl.description: Cookie-transport session lifetime (amendment §A1; OQ #2 resolved 2026-07-29): deliberately shorter than the bearer TTL — a browser session is likelier left open on an unattended screen.

password.description: Argon2id cost (RFC 0039 §C). Stored hashes verify under their own embedded parameters and re-hash to this cost on next successful login.

argon2_memory_kib.description: Memory cost in KiB. The 8 MiB floor rejects configurations weak enough to defeat the KDF's purpose.

argon2_parallelism.description: Lanes. Bounded by the argon2 encoding's uint8.

login_throttle.description: The amendment §B login limiters — live under BOTH auth modes, with the endpoint they defend. Two limiters because there are two keys (§B1): per_source is the Argon2id-amplification flood defence; per_username is the targeted-guessing defence. Each gets its own tracked-key LRU (§B2 — never the agent limiter's).

trusted_proxies.description: Reverse proxies (CIDRs or bare IPs) whose X-Forwarded-For is believed when resolving the per-source limiter key (amendment §B3). Empty: the TCP peer is always the source; behind a proxy the per-source limiter then degrades to a global one and the orchestrator WARNs at startup under `enabled`.

limiter.description: One sliding-window login limiter (its own RateLimitConfig instance). Defaults ratified 2026-07-29: per_source 10/60s, per_username 5/60s, each with a 1000-key LRU.

calls_per_window.description: Maximum admitted login attempts per key within the rolling window.

window_seconds.description: Rolling window length in seconds; also the 429's Retry-After value.

max_tracked.description: Tracked-key LRU bound. Eviction emits the existing telemetry-class audit event — the operator's cardinality-blow-up signal (§B2).
